text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index ended a week of constant retreat with another heavy fall, tumbling below the 4,600 level in late trade as index futures dived and dragged down the cash market. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,593.9, down 59.8 points, or 1.29 percent. This was 189.2 points down from last Friday.

FRANKFURT - Shares raced to early gains in bourse dealings and held on to most of the advance in moderate activity tied to the "triple witching" expiry of DAX futures, DAX options and stock options. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,788.27, up 39.00 points, or 1.04 percent, a rise of 43.83 on the week. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,788.54, up 10.98 points, or 0.29 percent.

PARIS - Stocks rose sharply as investors gave the new Socialist-led government the benefit of the doubt after what was viewed as a prudent keynote policy speech by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Thursday. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,757.10, up 17.41 points, or 0.64 percent, a fall of 51.42 from last week.

ZURICH - Shares closed at a third straight record high in both the blue-chip and broad indexes as gains in several high-profile stocks propelled the market. The Swiss market index closed at 5,561.8, up 51.5 points, or 0.93 percent and up 177.2 on the week.

MILAN - The bourse ended one percent up on the day with volumes at record levels after the expiry of options and futures and amid general optimism on the outlook for Italy, brokers said. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,185, up 127 points, or 0.97 percent, up 424 points on the week.
AMSTERDAM - Shares jumped to a new record after June option expiry took effect at 1400 GMT. The AEX index closed at 862.20, up 5.61 points, or 0.65 percent. There was a rise of 16.11 from last week.

TOKYO - Stocks ended with losses as investors squared positions ahead of the weekend and the G7 summit due to start later in the day, brokers said. They said the scandal involving Japanese brokers and racketeers also hurt the market, pressuring brokerage shares. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,385.54, down 122.31 points, or 0.60 percent. This was down 142.81 from last Friday.

HONG KONG - Stocks staged their biggest point gain in history, forging into record ground on a wave of handover euphoria to close at an all-time high. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,154.36, up 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent. A rise of 1,041.81 points on the week.

SYDNEY - A wave of confidence from overseas investors in Australia's resource and banking sectors carried local stocks to both a life-time high and a record close. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,712.6, up 19.3 points, or 0.72 percent, a rise of 57.30 from the previous Friday's close.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial shares braved an early buffetting at the hands of the futures market to power ahead and end the day firmly up on positive underlying sentiment, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,234.1, up 25.0 points, or 0.35 percent, down 37.4 from a week ago. The All Gold index closed at 1,027.4, down 33.9 points, or 0.92 percent, a drop of 101.6 since last week, while the Industrial index closed at 8,511.5, up 77.7 points, or 3.19 percent. This was up 29.1 from last Friday.
